sections.h2: Which Harrison office takes a Clare County deed?
sections.html:
The combined County Clerk and Register of Deeds office sits at 255 W. Main Street, Harrison, MI 48625. Mail goes to PO Box 438. Reach staff at 989-539-7131 or by fax at 989-539-6616, and the email address is clerk@clareco.net.

In Clare County one elected office holds both jobs, so the person who files circuit court papers and issues marriage licenses also keeps the land records. A seller in Clare, Farwell, Harrison or any lake community around them sends the deed to the same counter. Phone first for counter hours.

sections.h2: Who handles what in a home sale
sections.html:
The county records deeds and mortgages, while cities and townships handle tax assessment, building and zoning, and street maintenance. Ask the township or city office about assessments, and ask the Harrison office about what is on the record.

The office records the deed that moves ownership to your buyer and the mortgage that goes with it. It also holds earlier deeds, land contracts, discharges and liens, so a title search on a Clare County house begins and ends in these books. The clerk is also the county's official abstractor, which helps when a seller needs a title history on an older parcel. If you own an older wooded parcel, ask for the deed history early so closing is not held up.

  • Bring the original signed deed, not a photocopy.
  • Include the fee, a return envelope and any certificate the deed type requires.
  • Keep a copy of the recording stamp for your closing file.

Wooded acreage and lake cottages make up much of the housing stock around Harrison and Farwell, and many owners live elsewhere part of the year. When a deed has several co-owners who sign in different states, each signer's printed name must match the acknowledgment, so gather every signature page before the package goes to the recorder.

sections.h2: What Clare County charges to record a deed
sections.html:
The base charge set by Michigan is $30.00 a document, with page count irrelevant. MCL 600.2567 sends $5.00 of that fee into the register of deeds' automation fund and adds $3.00 for each additional instrument an assignment or discharge covers.

Copies run a dollar a page and a certification is $5.00. A requested records search costs 50 cents per year searched with a $5.00 floor, and filing some other paper is $1.00. Charter counties may use a different schedule, so verify the total with the Clare office by phone.

sections.h2: How transfer tax shows up on a Clare County deed
sections.html:
The deed must print the total value of the real property, or an affidavit of value goes with it. Both the county act (MCL 207.504) and the state act (MCL 207.525) require this.

With the value printed, the arithmetic is short. The county takes 55 cents and the state takes $3.75 on every $500 slice of price, partial slices counted whole. A $133,800 sale, which matches the typical home value in Clare County, spans 268 slices: $147.40 for the county and $1,005 for the state. If real and personal property sell together, naming each value separately confines the tax to the real property. Ask the office how it collects the tax so payment arrives with the deed.

sections.h2: What belongs on page one of a deed
sections.html:
The first printed line must name the recordable event in a single statement, such as warranty deed or quit claim deed. MCL 565.201 bars recording an instrument signed after April 1, 1997 when that statement points to more than one event.

  • Keep 2.5 inches clear at the head of page one.
  • Keep half an inch clear on every other side, on every page.
  • Print in 10-point type or larger, black ink, on white stock of 20-pound weight or more.
  • Attach nothing that falls outside letter or legal dimensions.

Once an instrument is received and recorded, the statute presumes it complies, so a clean first page protects you later.

sections.h2: When does a deed need treasurer certification?
sections.html:
A deed that conveys title with warranty covenants, and a land contract, needs county treasurer certification under MCL 211.135. The certificate says whether tax liens or tax titles exist and confirms payment of the taxes for the five years that precede the deed.

If the register of deeds refuses to receive a deed for lack of certificates, the office notes that fact on the instrument, and the person presenting it must obtain the certificate before trying again. Plan for that trip to the treasurer when you are scheduling a closing, because the deed cannot be recorded without it. A seller with back taxes should clear them first.

sections.h2: Recording a sale, step by step
sections.html:
A sale usually moves through the office in the same order. First, an attorney or title agent drafts the deed, and each seller signs with a printed name beneath the signature and a notary acknowledgment that matches. Second, if the deed warrants title, the Clare County Treasurer certifies the tax status, and any back taxes get paid at this point. Third, the closing agent figures the transfer tax from the full price and writes the check with the recording fee.

Fourth, the package goes to Harrison with the original deed, the fee and a return envelope, either by hand or by mail to PO Box 438. The office records the deed, adds it to the index and sends the recorded original back. Keep the recording stamp with your closing papers.

A cash sale to a buyer without a lender skips the mortgage recording, so only the deed and its fees are in play. The deed still has to meet every format rule on page one, and the tax certificate still applies if the deed carries warranty covenants. Ask your closing agent which of these apply before you sign, and ask the Harrison office if anything is unclear.

If the office returns a deed, fix the listed problem and bring it back. Phone first so you know the amount due.

sections.h2: Clare County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Clare County is a lower-priced market, with a large share of seasonal and part-year homes.

faqs.q: Is the Clare County Register of Deeds a separate office from the clerk?
faqs.a: No. The County Clerk and Register of Deeds offices are combined in Clare County, and both operate from 255 W. Main Street in Harrison.

faqs.q: How do I phone the Clare County office?
faqs.a: Dial 989-539-7131, or fax 989-539-6616. Letters go to PO Box 438, Harrison, MI 48625. Ask about counter hours before you deliver a deed.

faqs.q: What is the standard recording fee in Clare County?
faqs.a: The statutory fee is $30.00 per document, long or short. Add $3.00 for each extra instrument on an assignment or discharge, and $5.00 if you want a certified copy.

faqs.q: How do I figure the transfer tax on a Clare County sale?
faqs.a: Divide the price by $500, round up, then multiply by $0.55 for the county and by $3.75 for the state. A $150,000 sale is 300 slices, so $165 county tax plus $1,125 state tax, or $1,290 together.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Clare County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the signed original, the exact fee and a return envelope to PO Box 438, Harrison, MI 48625. Confirm the amount by phone first so the deed is not held for a short payment.
